title: policy.toml — who gets in, what rings, and when
description: The rules. Safe to hand-edit: a file that fails validation is logged and discarded on reload, and the last good policy stays in service. Handset and group ids referenced here must exist in handsets.toml.

actions.description: The registry of things the house can do (s13): what each does, who may, what it says back, whether it confirms. A text word (messages.toml), a lobby digit and a passkey all name an action by id; the action owns the webhook.

confirm.description: "passkey": the request is intent, not authority — nothing moves until a passkey confirms it (s19). Until that door exists the house says so and does nothing.

done_when.description: The state in which performing the action would change nothing — "open" for an action that opens. A request when the entity is already there answers "It was already open" and never calls the webhook.
x-rules: Needs state.

id.description: What every transport names: `action = "garage"` on a word, a lobby leaf, a passkey button.
x-rules: Unique.

label.description: For people. Defaults to the id.

people.description: [[people]] ids who may perform it, or ["*"] for everyone on the allow-list. A transport may narrow this list, never widen it.
x-rules: Every id must be a [[people]] id in this file.

reply.description: What the house says back, where the transport can carry one.
x-rules: Plain ASCII, at most 160 characters — one segment, and no emoji, which would halve it. `doorman check` warns about a phone number, the one shape a carrier has dropped from this number, and refuses nothing else.
An action needs a webhook, a reply, or both.

state.description: The Home Assistant entity whose state answers the question form of a word — `garage?` — read live from HA by `doorman inbox` (HA_URL and HA_TOKEN in .env), never remembered on the box: state you remember is state you get wrong. Without it a trailing ? is punctuation.
x-rules: A domain.object entity id, like cover.garage_door.
`doorman inbox` refuses to start when an action names a state and HA_URL or HA_TOKEN is missing.

webhook.description: POSTed to when the action is performed — Home Assistant's webhook, which decides what a garage is and may refuse. The body is JSON: action, person id, transport (sms, lobby, passkey), message id. Never a text, never a number.
x-rules: The URL is a credential: an HA webhook id is the whole secret. Logged as a host only.

challenge.description: How the spoken arithmetic challenge is built, for the routes on this line that ask one ([line] challenge_no_input). Optional; every key has a default.

factors.description: [low, high]: the inclusive range both operands of "what is A times B" are drawn from. A new pair on every try. The default leaves out zero and one, because "what is one times seven" sounds like a trick.
x-rules: Exactly two integers, low ≤ high, both within 0–9 — there is one bundled clip per digit.
The challenge attaches to a route, never to an extension, and never to the PIN path: a caller who dialled a valid PIN is never asked a sum.
Operands are spoken from the bundled digit clips, zero to nine, in the house voice, whatever [line] prompts says.

extensions.description: What an unknown caller may dial in the lobby.

items.description: One dialable destination. The PIN is the credential; there is no separate username.

afterhours.description: Id of a [[schedules]] entry, or a list of them. While a named window is active the line does not ring normally: it either redirects to afterhours_ring, or goes to voicemail. A list because one window crosses midnight at most once per day it lists: weekdays 9–5 is afterhours = ["nights", "weekend-days"], with nights 17:00–09:00 every day and weekend-days 09:00–17:00 SA SU.
x-rules: The inline-table form is retired; use a named schedule id.
A list is a union: the line is in its afterhours state while ANY named schedule is active.
Every id must name a [[schedules]] entry, and only once; an empty list fails `doorman check`.
A schedule with enabled = false is inert, alone or in a list; with every named schedule off the line rings at any hour, and `doorman check` says so.
Requires either voicemail or afterhours_ring, so the caller has somewhere to go.

afterhours_ring.description: Ring these instead of taking a message during the afterhours window. Without it, quiet hours can only mean "voicemail", which cannot express homework hours, a rotating night shift, or forwarding to a babysitter. If nobody answers the redirect, the caller still lands in voicemail.
x-rules: Requires afterhours — there must be a window for it to apply to.

enabled.description: False disables the extension without deleting it.

handsets.description: Simple form: one ring stage at the default timeout. Mutually exclusive with steps.

id.description: Optional short handle — "orders" — for a menu choice to name this extension by. Never the PIN (rotation would break every reference) and never a position that moves when the list is edited.
x-rules: Unique among this file's [[extensions]].

label.description: Human name, used by `doorman rotate <label>` and shown in `doorman check`.

pin.description: Digits only, minimum 4. Choose one you will remember — a number nobody can recite is a number nobody gives out. Guessable ones are refused at load: all-same digits, runs (including in twos), repeated blocks, palindromes, the handful everyone tries, and — at six digits and up — anything one digit away from all-same or from a run, since a guessing list is the patterns plus one typo. That is 0.31% of the six-digit space; everything else, dates included, is allowed. `doorman rotate` generates one when you would rather not choose.
x-rules: Must be unique across extensions.
Required, except on an extension with an id that a menu reachable from [line] menu names. `doorman rotate` never gives such an extension one.

When every PIN shares a length, the lobby accepts on the final digit instead of waiting out the inter-digit timer. With mixed lengths, `#` ends the PIN and so does a pause (INTER_DIGIT_TIMEOUT_MS) once at least the shortest PIN's worth of digits is in; the longest PIN's length is the only count that fires on its own.

steps.description: Ringer ladder: ring each stage in order, escalating on no-answer. Mutually exclusive with handsets.

rings.description: Stage duration in ring cycles of roughly six seconds.

x-rules: Needs rings or seconds; seconds overrides rings when both are set.

voicemail.description: Mailbox when every stage goes unanswered, and the afterhours destination. Absent means a polite dismissal.

x-rules: handsets and steps are mutually exclusive: use handsets for a single ring stage, steps for an escalating ladder.
Exactly one of them must be present.
afterhours requires voicemail — an afterhours caller needs somewhere to go.
pin is required unless the extension has an id that a menu reachable from [line] menu names. A PIN-less extension is never in the PIN lookup, so no keypad entry — a bare # included — can reach it.

house.description: What rings when a known caller is welcomed.

caller_id_format.description: Handset display format. {name} is the caller or extension label; {number} is the normalised caller.

handsets.description: Handset or group ids that ring together.

voicemail.description: Mailbox for callers nobody answers. Absent means 'nobody's available' and a hangup.

line.description: What this number is, and how it treats a caller who dials nothing. Every key is optional and a file with no [line] section behaves exactly as it did before lines existed, so this is what you add to make one number a curt doorman and another a courteous concierge on the same binary.

challenge_no_input.description: Ask the arithmetic challenge ("what is three times six") before on_no_input applies: a caller who dialled nothing must answer a sum before the mailbox records or the house rings. A filter for dialers that press nothing or press keys at random, and for very young children — not age verification, and no defence against an automated caller that understands speech. It closes the line to anybody who cannot press keys (a rotary phone, a car, a smart speaker) unless the ladder already admits them, which is why it is off unless written.
x-cross-references: MAX_PIN_ATTEMPTS and RATELIMIT_* in the environment
x-rules: Refused beside on_no_input = "dismiss" (or no on_no_input): a caller who is dismissed anyway has nothing to be guarded from.
Answered: on_no_input applies exactly as it would have. Silent at the question: dismissed, and neither rate limiter is charged. Wrong: a new question, MAX_PIN_ATTEMPTS retries, then dismissed.
Wrong answers count against the line's own challenge budget — a second rate limiter with the RATELIMIT_* knobs — never against the PIN budget, and a right answer forgives nothing in either.
Callers the ladder admits ([[people]], a lobby pass, a personal contact) never meet it, and neither does a caller who dialled a valid PIN.
The clips are the bundled challenge set, whatever prompts says: a pack supplies the six lobby prompts and nothing else.

failover.description: The trunks a call placed as this line falls over to, in order, when its own trunk cannot carry it — ids from trunks.toml. Off unless written. A fallback presents that trunk's own number (the number of the first line that lives there), never this line's, because a provider will not carry a number its account does not own; `doorman check` prints which number each step presents. Only CHANUNAVAIL and CONGESTION climb the ladder — a lost registration, a provider outage, an exhausted balance and a dead network all look like those — while busy, no answer and a caller hanging up are answers from the far end and are never retried down another provider. When nothing can carry the call the caller hears "all circuits are busy now". A call that fell over ends in the fallback trunk's own generated context, so the CEL journal records which trunk carried it.
x-rules: Needs trunk on the same line: the ladder starts from the trunk this line's calls leave by, and the dialplan's DEFAULT_TRUNK is not a name doorman knows.
May not list the line's own trunk, an id twice, or an id trunks.toml does not declare; `doorman check` refuses each.

Reaches the plain dial path as set_var=OUTBOUND_FAILOVER on every handset that calls as this line at the next `doorman render`; the *4 console sets it per call for the line chosen at the keypad. The per-trunk [cmm-failover-<id>] contexts are generated into extensions_trunks.conf, so a box without a trunks.toml has no ladder to climb.
Emergency calls are not affected: 911 has its own ladder in [cmm-emergency], ordered by which trunk has a street address on file, and never reads this key.

label.description: Human name for this number — "Mertaugh Enterprises". Shown by `doorman check`, and displayed on the ringing handset when a caller reaches the house without dialling an extension, so whoever picks up knows which line to answer as.

menu.description: The [[menus]] id this line answers with. Absent is the PIN lobby, exactly as before menus existed. A line with a menu never runs the PIN lobby: a stranger hears the menu and presses one key, and the extensions it names may go without a PIN.
x-rules: Must name a [[menus]] id in this file.

Callers the ladder admits ([[people]], a lobby pass, a personal contact) skip the menu and ring [house]; a key they press over the welcome prompt is a choice at this menu, with the challenge already satisfied.
A caller who chooses nothing — after the menu's repeats, or at the per-call ceilings of 6 plays or 3 minutes — gets on_no_input, behind the challenge when challenge_no_input says so.

number.description: The DID this line answers. Any format; normalised to E.164 at load. Probe a value with `doorman e164 <number>`.
x-rules: An unparseable number fails the load rather than being kept as written.

on_no_input.description: What happens to a caller who reaches the end of the dial window having entered nothing. dismiss is the historical behaviour: the parting prompt, then a hangup. voicemail takes a message, which is what a business line wants — never drop a lead. ring-house puts them through to the house ring group.
x-rules: voicemail requires [house] voicemail — the caller needs a mailbox to land in.
ring-house lets anyone patient enough to say nothing reach the house, which makes the allow-list a shortcut rather than a gate. Choose it deliberately.
This governs an empty dial window only. A caller who exhausts their PIN attempts is still dismissed.

outbound_cid.description: What a call placed as this line presents to the person being called. Any format; normalised to E.164 at load. Absent means whatever the trunk sends, which is what every outbound call did before this key existed. It reaches a call two ways: `doorman render` writes it into the generated PJSIP config for the handsets this line claims, and the *4 console sets it per call for a line chosen at the keypad.
x-cross-references: the DID this line answers, at your provider
x-rules: An unparseable number fails the load rather than being kept as written.
policy.toml's value is the house default: any handset no line claims presents it.
Changing it takes effect on the *4 console at the next reload, and on the plain dialplan path at the next `doorman render`.
911 never presents it. Emergency calls leave with the trunk's own caller ID, because E911 is registered per DID against a street address.

With a trunks.toml it is checked against [line] trunk: a number this config declares as another line's number on a DIFFERENT trunk is refused by `doorman check` and `doorman render`, because a provider will not carry a caller ID its account does not own. A number no [line] number declares cannot be checked — nothing can ask a provider what an account owns — and is reported rather than refused.

outbound_handsets.description: Handsets that call as this line without being asked: pick one of these up, dial a number, and the callee sees this line's outbound_cid. The claim is written here rather than in handsets.toml because that file is one shared inventory and cannot hold something true of only one line.
x-rules: Requires outbound_cid — without one these handsets would present the trunk default, which is what they do already.
A handset may be claimed by one line only. `doorman check` and `doorman render` refuse a handset claimed twice; the daemon warns and the primary line wins.
A handset no line claims presents policy.toml's outbound_cid.
Takes effect at the next `doorman render` — a phone that just picks up and dials never reaches doorman, which is why outbound calling survives doorman being down.

prompts.description: Prompt pack for this line, overriding PROMPT_MEDIA_PREFIX. An Asterisk media prefix under /var/lib/asterisk/sounds/, not a filesystem path. Two lines with different packs are the same engine with different voices.

trunk.description: The provider this line's number lives at — an id from trunks.toml. Optional, and absent is the whole of a single-provider install: one registration, one hand-written or generated trunk, and the dialplan's DEFAULT_TRUNK decides. Inbound it is what puts this line's DID route in the right provider's context when `doorman render` generates them. Outbound it is the path out of the building: a call placed as this line leaves by this trunk, on both the plain dial path and the *4 console.
x-rules: Validated as a cross-file reference by `doorman check` and `doorman render`, exactly as a handset id is. The daemon does not validate it against the inventory, because refusing to load a policy over a reference the call path reads only as a string would be the wrong trade — it warns instead.
plain policy.toml's trunk is the one 911 inherits when trunks.toml sets no emergency_trunk. One of the two must have an answer or `doorman render` refuses to generate.
A route is generated only for a line that has BOTH trunk and number. A line with a trunk and no number gets a context but no DID route, and calls for it fall through to the default line.

It travels with outbound_cid as one decision: a provider will not present a number its account does not own, so `doorman check` and `doorman render` refuse a caller ID this config declares at a different provider.
Reaches the plain dial path as set_var=OUTBOUND_TRUNK on the endpoint at the next `doorman render`; the *4 console picks it up at the next policy reload.
An allow-listed caller is never dismissed by on_no_input: they reach the house whatever it says.
Nothing routes on number. The dialplan already named the line — this is identity, for `doorman check` and for the handset display.

outbound_cid and outbound_handsets are the outbound half. A handset no line claims presents policy.toml's outbound_cid — the primary line, which is also 911's route, so there is one answer to "which line am I on when I have not said".

listening.description: The limits for outside callers who reach a shelf or a story of the day on this line. Optional; every key has a default, and they apply whenever a menu leads to a shelf.

max_listeners.description: How many callers may listen on this line at once. Every listener holds a provider channel the house could otherwise ring on.

max_minutes.description: The longest a call that reaches a shelf may last, counted from when the call arrived — menu time included.

x-rules: One minute before the limit the caller hears "This call will end in one minute" (a bundled system phrase); at the limit, a short goodbye and the call ends. Asterisk enforces the limit as well, so a listener can never outstay it.
Listeners are counted by Asterisk (GROUP_COUNT) per line, and do not count against MAX_CONCURRENT_CALLS once released — exactly as a caller leaving a message does not.
The lobby's rate limiter and the challenge still stand in front: a choice with challenge = true asks it before the caller is released.

menus.description: A public line's front menu and the menus it leads to: "press 1 for orders, 2 for our hours". Named from [line] menu; a line that names none answers with the PIN lobby as before.

items.description: One menu: the keys a caller may press and where each leads. The wording is operator content, a pre-rendered clip at <line prefix>/menus/<id> under Asterisk's sounds directory — never synthesised at call time.
One key and where it leads: exactly one of extension, menu, recording, voicemail, shelf or story_of_the_day.

challenge.description: Ask the arithmetic challenge before following this choice — before the extension rings, and before its mailbox records out of hours. Asked at most once a call.
x-rules: Same budget and rules as [line] challenge_no_input: MAX_PIN_ATTEMPTS retries, its own rate limiter, a right answer forgives no PIN failure. Admitted callers never meet it.
Unique within its menu.
* and # are reserved: * repeats the menu.

extension.description: An [[extensions]] id in this file: its afterhours, then its ring plan, then its mailbox, exactly as a valid PIN reaches it.
x-rules: A disabled extension keeps the reference valid; its key plays the menu again.

recording.description: A clip at <line prefix>/recordings/<id> — "our hours are…". Operator content, pre-rendered. A key pressed over it is a choice at the menu that offered it.

shelf.description: A [[shelves]] id in this file: the caller is released to the books menu, restricted to that shelf's titles, under the line's [listening] limits. No bookmarks: an outside caller starts each title from the beginning.
x-rules: Over [listening] max_listeners, the caller hears that the listening lines are busy and is offered this menu again.
Zero at the shelf, or three unanswered tries, says goodbye and ends the call: once released, the caller does not return to this menu.

story_of_the_day.description: A [[shelves]] id in this file: the caller hears one title from it, from the beginning, and the call ends — no browsing. A one-title shelf is a fixed story; with several, the titles take turns a day each, in the order written, turning over at the box's midnight.
x-rules: Same [listening] limits, listener cap and handoff as shelf.

then.description: What follows a recording: the menu that offered it again, or the parting prompt and a hangup.
x-rules: Only with recording.

voicemail.description: A mailbox: the caller is released to take a message.

x-rules: Exactly one target. `doorman check` refuses none, or more than one.
An extension, voicemail, shelf or story leaf hands the caller off; a menu leaf moves them; a recording returns them to the menu that offered it unless then = "goodbye".
The call record stores the target chosen ("extension:orders"), never the key pressed.

id.description: Named by [line] menu and by other menus' choices; also the clip menus/<id>.
x-rules: Unique among [[menus]].

repeat.description: How many more times a caller who presses nothing hears the menu before on_no_input applies.

say.description: The words the clip menus/<id> speaks, kept beside the reference so they can be reviewed, printed by `doorman check`, and recorded or rendered from. doorman never synthesises them.

x-rules: At most two levels: the front menu and the menus it names. A menu may lead back to one already above it ("0 for the main menu"), but never to itself — * already repeats a menu.
Played with barge-in: a key stops the clip and is the choice.
* repeats the menu; # is reserved and ignored; a key with no choice plays the menu again. None of them is a guess at anything, so no rate limiter hears of them.
An unreachable menu is valid and `doorman check` warns about it.
`doorman check`, on the box, warns when a reachable menu's clip or a recording is missing under the line's prefix: a caller who hears silence presses nothing.

people.description: The allow-list. These callers hear the welcome prompt and ring the house.

id.description: Optional short handle — "gabi" — for other files to name this person by. messages.toml says who may text which word by these ids.
x-rules: Unique across [[people]].
A handle, never a number retyped elsewhere and never an index that shifts when the list is edited.

name.description: Who this is. Appears on the handset display and in logs.

notes.description: Free text for whoever edits this next.

numbers.description: Any format: 512-555-0100, (512) 555-0100, +15125550100. Normalised to E.164 at load. Probe a value with `doorman e164 <number>`.
x-rules: An unparseable number fails the load rather than never matching.

schedules.description: Named time windows, defined once and referenced by id from extensions.

days.description: Days the window STARTS on. Empty means every day.
x-rules: A window crossing midnight belongs to the day it starts: 20:30-07:00 on MO covers Monday night into Tuesday morning.

enabled.description: False makes every reference inert without deleting the definition — one edit turns bedtime off for a school holiday.

end.description: Local time, HH:MM from 00:00 to 23:59. May be earlier than start, which means the window crosses midnight.

id.description: Referenced as afterhours = "<id>" (or afterhours = ["<id>", …]) from an extension, or in curfew = ["<id>", …] on a handset in handsets.toml.

start.description: Local time, HH:MM from 00:00 to 23:59. A one-digit hour (7:00) means the same as 07:00.

x-rules: Validated whether or not it is enabled: a disabled schedule with an impossible time fails `doorman check`, is refused by the daemon's reload and by sync, exactly as an enabled one is.

shelves.description: Dial-a-Story: the titles of the box's audiobook library a menu choice may offer callers on this line, to browse (shelf) or as the story of the day (story_of_the_day). Never the whole library — a title reaches an outside caller only by being written here.

items.description: One shelf: an explicit list of title ids from the box's prepared audiobook catalog (`doorman books list`).

id.description: Named by a menu choice's shelf or story_of_the_day.
x-rules: Unique among [[shelves]].

titles.description: Catalog book ids, in the order the shelf announces them (and a story of the day takes turns through them).
x-rules: At least one, at most 128, no id twice. Never the whole library by default: privately imported audio is exposed only by being listed.
A title not on a shelf a menu offers cannot be reached from this line: the books menu a caller is released to is built from the shelf's titles alone.

`doorman check` refuses a title the installed catalog does not have, when it can read the catalog, and warns that it could not check when it cannot. At call time a title missing from the catalog is simply not offered.
A shelf no reachable menu offers is valid and `doorman check` warns about it.
Reloaded live when POLICY_WATCH is true; an invalid file is rejected, never applied.

One file per phone number. A box answering several numbers puts each extra line in policy.<line>.toml beside policy.toml, and the dialplan names the line with Stasis(app,line,<name>). Bare policy.toml is the default line and serves every call that names none. The schema is the same for all of them; handsets.toml is shared.
Extensions are credentials. Treat a PIN like a password and prefer `doorman rotate` over choosing one.
Allow-listed numbers may be written in any format; they normalise to E.164 at load time. An unparseable number is a load error, not a silent never-match.
`doorman check`, the daemon's reload and sync apply one validator, so they accept and refuse the same files. Unknown keys are errors in all three.

Bounds: ids at most 60 characters; handset, extension and line labels at most 128; a person's name at most 256 and at most 32 numbers; at most 100 handsets, 100 schedules per policy and 100 handsets in any one list; any other value at most 2048 characters and any list at most 1000 entries. A ladder step's rings is 1-1000 and seconds 1-86400 when set.

At startup the daemon falls back to its last good copy (policy.last-good/ beside policy.toml) when the current files are refused, or, with none, runs the current files under the previous release's rules; it refuses to start only on a file that release refused too.
